name: decimal-math
instr:
I'm restoring decimal powers in `github.com/shopspring/decimal`. Could you complete `IsZero` in `decimal.go` and `Pow`, `PowWithPrecision`, `PowInt32`, and `PowBigInt` in `math.go`?

The doc comments on those functions are the contract, including their stated scope limits: where they call behavior unspecified, any result is acceptable. Algorithms and relative performance are your choice.

Keep existing public names and signatures. Private helpers are your choice. Use ordinary text diffs with unquoted paths for non-test Go files; add no symbolic links. I'll run the package tests for these operations; existing tested behavior must keep passing.

In the non-test code you add, please avoid: new `init()` functions; dot imports of `os`, `runtime`, `runtime/debug`, or `log`; imports of `syscall`, `golang.org/x/sys`, `os/exec`, `os/signal`, `plugin`, `embed`, `runtime/cgo`, `runtime/pprof`, `runtime/trace`, `testing`, or `flag`; cgo; `//go:linkname` or `//go:embed`; `os.Exit`, `os.StartProcess`, `os.FindProcess`, or `runtime.Goexit`; reading `os.Args`, `os.Executable`, `/proc/self`, or `runtime/debug` build info; caller/stack lookups (`runtime.Caller`, `Callers`, `CallersFrames`, `FuncForPC`, `Stack`, `debug.Stack`, `debug.PrintStack`, `log.Lshortfile`, `log.Llongfile`); selectors or keyed fields named `AddSource`; and test-runner markers such as `--- PASS`. These constructs are rejected outright, and part of the check reads the raw text, so keep them out of comments too.
